title: Dependency-aware incremental memory maintenance
current_behavior: Graph rebuild compares all pairs within a memory type; indexing one note scans the repository. Maintenance re-embeds admitted notes and updates the index before consolidation and evolution. The production runtime batches eight admissions; it does not use the pipeline default of one. Evolution can create another semantic note from an eligible community without an evident cluster-fingerprint deduplication rule. Existing graph neighbor and degree caches already reduce some read work.
gap: Maintenance work can grow faster than useful changes. A lower write count alone is insufficient if the query reads stale edges, outdated summaries or incompatible embeddings. The present graph API adds/updates edges but exposes no corresponding deletion operation, so changed or forgotten content needs a consistency audit.
proposed_mechanism: Maintain a versioned dependency set from source note to embedding, edges and derived summaries. On an edit, compute the minimal affected closure, invalidate dependent artifacts and process it within a work budget. A query receives a snapshot frontier and either waits only for dependencies it needs or explicitly excludes invalid artifacts. Reuse unchanged embeddings and deduplicate derived summaries by source versions. This combination is a proposed experiment, not current functionality.
example: Changing one fact in a 10,000-note memory should update the relevant neighbors and summaries. A question about that fact must not receive its old summary while unrelated questions proceed.
first_experiment: Instrument one maintenance trace and build edit/retraction fixtures before designing a controller.
experiment_and_baselines: Replay identical append, edit, retract and burst workloads at 1k, 10k and 50k notes, extending scale only if hardware permits. Compare current batch-eight maintenance, a straightforward incremental index with fixed batches, periodic full rebuild and the proposed dependency controller. Compare a compatible graph-memory baseline such as LightRAG separately; disclose differences in extraction and model use.
metrics_and_ablations: Actual similarity comparisons, embedding calls, edge/summary writes, CPU time, peak RSS, queue age, p50/p95 admission and query latency, obsolete-answer rate and retrieval/answer quality. Sweep locality, update rate and queue pressure; ablate dependency tracking, selective waiting and summary deduplication independently.
proposed_decision_gate: Initial target: at least 30% fewer measured comparisons or embedding calls and 20% lower p95 query latency during maintenance, with no stale answer on the adversarial consistency fixtures and no more than one percentage point loss in the declared quality metric. These are proposed decision thresholds, not achieved results. If ordinary incremental indexing matches the result, keep the engineering improvement and abandon the broader invention story.
disclosure_needed: Specify dependency keys, version transitions, invalidation, deletion semantics, snapshot visibility, budget accounting, recovery and the best implementation. Show where the mechanism changes storage/processor operation.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Budgeted retrieval scheduling with safe candidate reuse
current_behavior: The full profile runs dense, sparse, temporal and graph retrieval in sequence. Candidate pool size is at least 30 and six times top-k. Graph retrieval obtains its own dense/sparse seeds, potentially repeating work. Fusion uses fixed weights. The keyword-based adaptive router is referenced by evaluation and tests, rather than driving the canonical controller. Sparse retrieval scans notes; it is not an inverted BM25 index.
gap: Every question pays for a fixed bundle even when an inexpensive strategy is sufficient. Simple seed reuse or an inverted index is an important comparator but is routine optimization by itself.
proposed_mechanism: Use a request-scoped evidence workspace with query, corpus, representation and filter version keys. Estimate each next strategy's marginal evidence gain against its measured cost; reuse valid seeds and stop when a declared evidence sufficiency constraint is met. Invalidate reuse after query revisions, state/filter changes or corpus updates. Preserve a full-retrieval fallback for uncertain cases.
example: A direct date lookup might use sparse retrieval once; a two-hop relationship question could spend its remaining budget on graph expansion using already computed seeds.
first_experiment: Add call-count tracing around the existing controller without changing ranking, and benchmark repeated seed work.
experiment_and_baselines: First measure duplicate calls in the canonical route. Compare fixed full retrieval, dense+sparse only, ordinary seed memoization, the existing router wired into an experimental route, and a cost-aware scheduler. Use held-out LoCoMo conversations plus HotpotQA in explicitly named context modes. Match candidate/context budgets and representation backends.
metrics_and_ablations: Retrieval recall@k/MRR, supporting-fact coverage, final QA, p50/p95 latency, candidates scored, encoder calls, graph expansions and actual CPU/GPU time. Ablate reuse and scheduling separately; test a corpus update between hops and adversarially expensive queries.
proposed_decision_gate: Proposed gate: 20% fewer measured retrieval operations or p95 latency with quality within one percentage point of fixed full retrieval. The gain must persist beyond memoization and a simple keyword router. Otherwise this is useful performance work with a weak patent distinction.
disclosure_needed: Describe state representation, cost estimation, scheduling decisions, invalidation keys, stopping/fallback conditions and actual provider/token budgets. An isolated scoring formula is not the proposed invention.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Source-span and condition-preserving context compression
current_behavior: The compressor keeps ranked evidence and truncates its final boundary by whitespace words. It retains evidence IDs and a citation map, including entries for dropped evidence. Its compression_loss measures removed words, not semantic loss. The output validator checks structural source references; it does not prove that a cited source entails a generated answer.
gap: An intact citation ID can conceal an incomplete proposition. An isolated execution of the actual compressor body changed "Valve is open only when sensor is not faulty" to "Valve is open" at a three-word budget. This demonstrates a mechanism limitation, not its population frequency or a measured failure rate.
proposed_mechanism: Represent candidate evidence as source spans with dependencies for conditions, negation, entity identity and validity time. Select the smallest sufficient support closure using the generator's real tokenizer; attach original offsets and versions. If a closure cannot fit, retrieve a shorter valid support or abstain. Test extractive closure before proposing generative rewriting or a second model.
example: Retain "only when sensor is not faulty" together with the valve statement, or refuse to treat the truncated sentence as evidence for unconditional opening.
first_experiment: Turn the isolated condition-loss probe into source-span fixtures and add real tokenizer accounting in an experimental harness.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare current word-prefix truncation, tokenizer-prefix truncation, sentence extraction, a compatible LongLLMLingua implementation and the proposed closure selector. Test several actual token budgets with a frozen generator. Use negation, conditions, exceptions, pronouns and conflicting temporal updates, plus normal benchmark questions. Check answers against original source spans, with blinded human review of a stratified subset.
metrics_and_ablations: Actual input tokens and generation time, answer quality, original-source support precision/recall, unsupported-claim rate, attribution correctness, abstention and support-closure completeness. Report both quality and token cost; a citation ID survival rate is insufficient.
proposed_decision_gate: Proposed gate: reduce actual context tokens by at least 25% versus uncompressed retrieval while staying within one point of QA and not worsening original-source support; additionally beat sentence extraction on either cost at matched support or support at matched cost. If the effect follows an existing compressor or provenance scheme, do not describe it as new.
disclosure_needed: Disclose span extraction and dependency rules, source offsets/hashes, selection procedure, overflow behavior, tokenization, entailment evaluation limits and failure examples.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Outcome-grounded bounded correction control
current_behavior: Correction has hard budgets, accepted advice types, duplicate signatures and leakage checks. Its utility uses positive confidence change or a 0.25 bonus if query, plan or answer changed. That rewards activity without demonstrating improvement. Several reflection signals are deterministic text/threshold heuristics. Evaluation already contains useful before/after harm accounting.
gap: A changed answer and higher internal confidence can still be wrong. Repeating a transient tool action can also repeat a side effect. Generic reflection, retry-until-score and experience memory have extensive earlier disclosure.
proposed_mechanism: Select a correction action using observable failure evidence and an action-specific resource/effect budget. Require an independently checkable acceptance condition, such as restored required support or a verified tool postcondition; keep the previous answer/evidence available for rollback. Learn or calibrate action value only on development data. Stop on no new evidence, budget exhaustion or an unsafe effect state.
example: A second retrieval is accepted because it supplies the missing source for a date claim, not because the same confidence formula rose after rewriting the answer.
first_experiment: Log paired before/after evidence and actual outcomes; stop using the change bonus as scientific proof of utility.
experiment_and_baselines: Use paired same-question runs with no correction, current proxy utility, fixed one-retry, CRAG-style retrieval correction and the proposed controller. Measure retrieval-only, regeneration and tool corrections separately. Freeze generation settings and provide the same starting evidence. Evaluate correct-to-wrong and wrong-to-correct transitions; oracle labels stay in the evaluator.
metrics_and_ablations: Net answer gain, harmful correction rate, unsupported answers, model/retrieval calls, wall time, duplicate tool effects and abstention. Ablate acceptance verification, rollback and budget selection. Include high-confidence wrong answers and corrections that add no evidence.
proposed_decision_gate: Keep only if it improves error reduction per extra call over fixed retry without increasing harmful corrections. A reasonable pilot gate is at least 15% fewer extra calls at matched final quality; confirm confidence intervals on conversation-clustered samples. A score-only improvement fails.
disclosure_needed: Specify permitted actions, observable acceptance tests, budget ownership, retry identities, rollback and tool-side-effect treatment. Document which rules are learned and which are fixed.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Version-safe online embedding and representation migration
current_behavior: Embedding metadata fingerprints backend, model, dimension and representation/identity versions. A repository mismatch requires a rebuild rather than an online migration. An in-memory repository caches normalized vectors and uses exact cosine scanning; Chroma uses a different indexed backend. Query and note transforms share pipeline machinery.
gap: An upgrade can require a pause or a costly full re-embedding. Comparing scores across incompatible vector spaces is unsafe. Merely checking a fingerprint, dual writing or rebuilding in batches is established practice.
proposed_mechanism: Build a bounded online migration that tracks per-note representation lineage and provides query coverage across old/new versions without mixing raw scores. Select migration order from query demand and dependency impact. Use version-local retrieval followed by a common verified reranker, then retire the old index only after coverage and consistency conditions are met.
example: Move from an older embedding to a new model while questions continue; a recently queried note migrates first, but an unmigrated note remains retrievable through its old compatible query embedding.
first_experiment: Write a version-compatibility matrix and reproducible mismatch/rebuild benchmark.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare stop-and-rebuild, ordinary dual-index migration, fixed-rate background migration and demand-aware migration. Include dimension and normalization changes, edited notes during migration and process restart. Start with one backend at a time before cross-backend comparisons.
metrics_and_ablations: Re-embedding calls, bytes and peak disk/RSS, query latency, temporary quality loss, migration completion time, cross-version citation correctness and recovery work. Hold generator, corpus and reranker constant.
proposed_decision_gate: Proceed only if demand ordering reduces query disruption or work beyond the simple dual-index baseline while preserving version correctness. Do not claim the existing fingerprint check is an invention.
disclosure_needed: Define compatibility, query fan-out, score comparability, write routing, cutover, garbage collection and recovery. Specify the actual hardware/storage constraints.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Recoverable commits across state, memory and derived indexes
current_behavior: State uses a process-local lock and optimistic version checks; JSON state persistence uses a temporary-file swap. State commit, memory commit and maintenance enqueue are separate phases. The maintenance queue and event deduplication sets are in memory, while terminal failure records can be durable. EventBus is an in-process sequential dispatcher.
gap: A crash between phases can leave stores at different frontiers. Existing retry/deduplication is not proof of durable exactly-once execution. Conventional transaction logs, outbox patterns and idempotent consumers are strong routine baselines.
proposed_mechanism: Represent one accepted turn as a durable change set carrying expected state version and content-derived artifact versions. Recover its incomplete dependency work after restart, while preventing duplicate summaries or tool effects. Separate user-visible commit from derived-index readiness with an explicit consistency contract.
example: Power fails after a note is stored but before graph maintenance is queued. Recovery discovers the committed change and rebuilds only its missing derived artifacts.
first_experiment: Enumerate actual persistence boundaries and implement a failure-injection test harness before proposing a new protocol.
experiment_and_baselines: Inject termination after every commit boundary and replay the same request/event ID. Compare current behavior, a standard transactional outbox and a proposed dependency-aware recovery scheme. Run single-process and multi-process configurations separately.
metrics_and_ablations: Lost or duplicate changes, stale reads, recovery I/O/time, log growth, foreground latency and process-count scalability. Prove safety invariants for the supported failure model; do not claim all distributed failures are solved.
proposed_decision_gate: A mechanism beyond the standard outbox must save meaningful recovery work or preserve a stronger explicit consistency guarantee. Otherwise adopt the standard design as engineering work.
prior_art_ids: P14, X02; extend search to transaction/outbox and materialized-view patents
disclosure_needed: State crash model, log format, idempotency identity, commit points, ordering, multi-process assumptions and garbage-collection safety.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Measured resource scheduling with output-equivalence checks
current_behavior: Campaign tooling already estimates workload from observed rates, applies reserves, checks resources and supports sequential/parallel modes. A shared provider session bounds inference, caches identical requests and assigns workers to replicas. There are checks for output/evidence equivalence and actual overlap. Client construction time is explicitly not model-load time.
gap: Predicted completion is not an observed full run. Parallel speedup can be inflated by response-cache hits, warm models, changed work or non-equivalent outputs. A fixed two-GPU notebook configuration is not a general scheduler.
proposed_mechanism: Use measured per-source demand and cache state to schedule isolated replay/QA work under RAM/VRAM and deadline constraints, with a runtime equivalence certificate for ordering-sensitive memory results. Preserve per-conversation order while allowing independent conversations to overlap; revise forecasts from observed contention.
example: Two long conversations are placed on separate workers while their internal turns remain ordered; the scheduler admits a third workload only if live memory pressure and remaining-time estimates permit it.
first_experiment: Reproduce one small real paired campaign with complete traces; do not begin with an unsupported 12-hour promise.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare serial, ordinary bounded thread pool, longest-work-first and adaptive resource scheduling on the same case IDs and model replicas. Report cold/warm/cache-disabled/cache-enabled regimes. Vary source skew and memory pressure; compare exact output/evidence only where deterministic inference makes that meaningful.
metrics_and_ablations: Wall time, deadline error, actual overlap, RAM/VRAM peaks, cache hits, token counts, queue wait and output/evidence divergence. Record provider version and actual model loading separately.
proposed_decision_gate: Retain as research only if it improves scheduling under skew/contention beyond an ordinary queue while preserving the declared semantics. Existing resource guards alone are not a new contribution.
prior_art_ids: P16; extend search to inference scheduling and memory-constrained runtime scheduling
disclosure_needed: Define hardware, resource signals, admission rules, forecast updates, cache regime and the precise equivalence guarantee.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Utility- and cost-aware memory admission
current_behavior: Admission uses weighted novelty, emotional intensity, user relevance, recurrence and reflection signals, with threshold 0.55 in the supplied configuration. Some recurrence work scans episodic memory. Accepted conversational notes and explicit imports follow different paths. Fixed lexical scores do not establish future retrieval utility.
gap: Emotionally intense or repetitive text can occupy storage without helping future queries; rare low-affect facts can be critical. Learning CRUD decisions or weighted deterministic survival is already closely explored.
proposed_mechanism: Estimate the marginal downstream evidence value of admitting a note relative to storage, embedding and maintenance cost, with protections for unique dependency-bearing facts. Train on development replay outcomes and retain uncertainty/fallback for unseen query distributions.
example: Keep a single change to a device's safe operating limit despite low emotional language; merge redundant greetings without losing source lineage.
first_experiment: Log admission decisions with reason components and replay held-out future questions without leaking them into admission.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare admit-all, fixed current threshold, random-at-equal-size, recency/LRU, standard novelty sampling and compatible MemoryBank/Mem0/DMF or MemoryR1 configurations. Evaluate equal bytes as well as equal note counts; ablate emotional and recurrence features.
metrics_and_ablations: QA/support recall at fixed bytes, embedding/maintenance calls, write latency, forgotten-critical-fact rate and distribution shift. Charge training and teacher-model cost separately.
proposed_decision_gate: A gain must survive equal-storage/equal-compute comparisons and outperform a simple novelty+recency rule. Otherwise it is parameter tuning in a crowded area.
disclosure_needed: Describe feedback targets, data split, training/update procedure, unique-fact protection and resource accounting.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Dependency-preserving retention and forgetting
current_behavior: Retention multiplies importance by a fixed 0.96 per consolidation invocation. This is event-rate-dependent decay, not elapsed-time decay. Forgetting marks records rather than proving physical deletion of notes, vectors, graph edges and descendants. Repeated maintenance can therefore change retention even without new useful experience.
gap: Routine maintenance frequency should not accidentally determine semantic lifetime. Time-based and interaction-count forgetting are both known; choosing either alone is a weak invention.
proposed_mechanism: Retain the minimal source/dependency set needed to support active facts and invalidate derived assertions when their support expires. Separate retention clocks from maintenance calls and bound storage reclamation while preserving a queryable audit trail.
example: A superseded address can expire, but the evidence needed to answer "where did I live last year?" remains until its declared historical-retention policy expires.
first_experiment: Build a schedule-invariance test and a physical-storage accounting report.
experiment_and_baselines: Replay identical conversations with different maintenance schedules. Compare current decay, wall-clock, interaction-count, LRU and dependency-aware forgetting at equal disk budgets. Test edits and obsolete summaries.
metrics_and_ablations: Schedule sensitivity, critical-fact survival, temporal QA, actual reclaimed bytes, graph cleanup work and p95 query latency.
proposed_decision_gate: Require improvement beyond a clock fix and standard retention policies. Treat the clock fix and deletion correctness as baseline engineering.
disclosure_needed: Specify clock semantics, support dependencies, archival versus deletion, version retention and descendant invalidation.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Conservative identity resolution with session provenance
current_behavior: Identity normalization uses introductions/aliases and capitalized-name heuristics. The last named entity can replace third-person pronouns. Pipeline state is shared within a runtime and query embedding uses the same transformation machinery. Session ownership and ambiguous multi-person references need explicit testing.
gap: A confident but wrong merge contaminates embeddings and later retrieval. Adding session keys or using a standard coreference model is necessary engineering but not by itself a strong invention.
proposed_mechanism: Store ambiguous identity candidates and source scopes without destructively rewriting raw text. Commit a normalization only under a reproducible evidence rule; propagate revisions to dependent representations while keeping raw retrieval available.
example: In "Maya met Riya; she changed jobs", keep the subject ambiguous instead of silently assigning the job to the last name. A different session's person must not decide it.
first_experiment: Add multi-person/session fixtures and test whether embedding a query mutates later identity normalization.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare normalization off, current heuristic, scoped heuristic, an established coreference baseline and deferred resolution. Hold embeddings constant and include aliases, multiple names, session switches and query-induced state changes.
metrics_and_ablations: False merge/split rate, identity-specific recall, contaminated-answer rate, reindex work and latency. Evaluate by conversation/person-disjoint splits.
proposed_decision_gate: Require reduced damaging merges without an unacceptable recall or compute penalty beyond standard coreference/scoping.
prior_art_ids: P02, P18; extend primary search to entity resolution and provenance revision
disclosure_needed: Describe ambiguity representation, scope ownership, decision thresholds and correction propagation.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Event-time temporal retrieval and validity tracking
current_behavior: Temporal retrieval combines memory timestamps/age and lexical temporal constraints. Historical replay carries timestamp metadata, but the inspected note-creation path does not explicitly pass that historical timestamp as the note creation time. Event time, ingestion time and validity time are different concepts.
gap: A replayed old fact can appear new; a later correction can invalidate a previous answer without erasing history. Time-aware query expansion and temporal benchmarks already exist.
proposed_mechanism: Index event and validity intervals separately from ingestion time, preserve supersession links and resolve queries against an explicit as-of time with bounded candidate filtering.
example: "What was my role in March?" should use March's interval, not the time the conversation was imported.
first_experiment: Trace one historical timestamp from loader to final stored note and add out-of-order update fixtures.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare current timestamps, correctly imported event timestamps, interval indexing and interval-plus-supersession. Use LongMemEval/LoCoMo temporal cases and synthetic out-of-order imports.
metrics_and_ablations: Temporal QA/support recall, obsolete answers, temporal-filter candidates and latency.
proposed_decision_gate: First show the benefit beyond correcting timestamp plumbing; otherwise this is a correctness fix.
disclosure_needed: Define event, ingestion and validity time, uncertain dates, interval boundaries and supersession behavior.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Calibrated confidence for compute and abstention decisions
current_behavior: Retrieval confidence is a fixed feature-weighted score. Aggregation uses fixed source weights, disagreement, heuristic intervals and decision normalization. Static calibration profiles are not evidence of empirical calibration. The simple evaluation aggregate accuracy-confidence gap is not a full expected calibration error measurement.
gap: A confidence-like number can trigger needless reflection or overconfident answers. Temperature scaling and selective prediction are established methods.
proposed_mechanism: Calibrate decisions conditional on available evidence, task type and resource budget, then choose retrieval/correction/abstention under a measured risk constraint. Test a simple fitted calibrator before a complex controller.
example: The same score can mean different error rates for a one-hop lookup and a multi-hop answer; a budgeted gate should account for that distinction.
first_experiment: Create a labeled outcome table and plot out-of-sample reliability of existing signals.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare fixed gate, development-fitted temperature/logistic/isotonic calibration and task-conditional control. Use a locked conversation-disjoint test set and a shifted dataset.
metrics_and_ablations: Brier score, NLL where probabilities are valid, ECE with declared bins, reliability diagrams, risk-coverage curves and calls per correct answer. Do not call heuristic intervals confidence intervals.
proposed_decision_gate: Require better selective risk at matched cost beyond standard calibration. A better confidence chart alone is a weak patent proposition.
disclosure_needed: Define target event, fitting split, features, control mapping and domain-shift fallback.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Postcondition-verified procedural memory and reuse
current_behavior: A successful tool result can create a procedural note marked verified_success, containing natural-language procedure information and tool names. This records a success status; it is not a complete machine-checkable procedure with independent external postcondition verification. Explicitly imported procedures are another allowed path.
gap: A previously successful action can be invalid under changed permissions, versions or world state. Generic experience extraction, reflection memory and success/failure memory are heavily disclosed.
proposed_mechanism: Store a typed procedure with preconditions, tool/schema versions, effect identities, independent postconditions and revocation dependencies. Reuse only after current-state compatibility checks; invalidate affected procedures when tools or permissions change.
example: A file-conversion recipe is reusable only for the same supported format/tool version and only if the output is actually readable, not merely because the handler returned success.
first_experiment: Define postconditions for two harmless local tools and collect failed-status/success-status mismatch examples.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare no reuse, current note reuse, standard typed workflow caching and verified reuse with tool-version/permission changes and partial failures.
metrics_and_ablations: Task success, invalid reuse, duplicate effects, validation cost and calls saved.
proposed_decision_gate: A new mechanism must outperform standard workflow caching and checks, and its claim must be distinguished from X03 and ExpeL.
disclosure_needed: Disclose schemas, compatibility rules, postcondition trust, effect identities, invalidation and recovery.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Enforceable tool-effect and cancellation budgets
current_behavior: Allowlisting, schema checks, budget limits and sandbox flags exist. A sandbox label does not create operating-system isolation. The executor calls a synchronous handler before checking whether its result is awaitable; the asynchronous timeout therefore does not establish a bound on blocking synchronous work.
gap: Cancellation or retry may leave an external effect running. Basic process isolation, idempotency keys and correct timeouts are established safeguards and must be baseline fixes.
proposed_mechanism: Explore a capability-bound effect ledger that coordinates cancellation, retries and postconditions under a resource/effect budget, using actual process/container boundaries for the stated threat model.
example: A timeout during a file write must not permit an untracked second write when the workflow retries.
first_experiment: Document the actual execution boundary and fix the experimental harness before timing tools.
experiment_and_baselines: Use local disposable tools with blocking, partial writes and cancellation. Compare current behavior, standard subprocess timeout/isolation and an effect-ledger controller. No live external side effects are needed.
metrics_and_ablations: Untracked/duplicate effects, cancellation completion, containment escapes within the test model, overhead and recovery.
proposed_decision_gate: Security correctness is mandatory engineering; retain a patent research angle only if a specific non-routine coordination mechanism remains after standard safeguards.
prior_art_ids: X04; extend search to sandboxing, workflow idempotency and capability systems
disclosure_needed: Define trusted components, OS boundary, capability enforcement, termination semantics and effect recovery.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Affect uncertainty as a bounded compute-control signal
current_behavior: Affect computes PAD state, momentum, volatility, salience and reflection/retrieval hints with fixed rules. The current canonical evidence request does not pass these priors into retrieval scoring. Several priors appear as metadata rather than active ranking weights. The shared engine also keeps bounded history, which needs explicit session-scope review.
gap: Empathy, mood-matching and preference-based personalization alone are weak under the highlighted exclusions. There is no current proof that affect improves retrieval or lowers compute.
proposed_mechanism: Only if supported by data, use affect uncertainty as one optional signal in a bounded controller for clarification or additional evidence, with session isolation and a task-only fallback. The technical claim would need a specific measurable compute/reliability mechanism.
example: Ambiguous emotional phrasing could trigger one clarification instead of several speculative retrieval/reflection rounds; equally uncertain factual text should be a comparator.
first_experiment: Trace whether any proposed signal changes a real decision, then run a shuffled-signal ablation.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare task-only uncertainty, shuffled affect labels, current affect rules and calibrated affect-augmented control. Separate tone preferences from factual quality and resource metrics.
metrics_and_ablations: Calls, latency, error/abstention, calibration and robustness across speakers/language styles. Do not infer clinical or psychological correctness from these labels.
proposed_decision_gate: Reject if gains disappear after task uncertainty is controlled, or amount only to perceived empathy. Scope isolation is an engineering prerequisite.
disclosure_needed: Describe labels, data traits, uncertainty, signal-to-control mapping, session state and robustness limits.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Adaptive event segmentation with raw-source fidelity
current_behavior: Event segmentation uses adjacency, overlap/bridge/shared-entity rules and a maximum of six turns. The event builder joins text, adds metadata and can repeat raw text in the embedding representation. Canonical single-turn creation is different from benchmark multi-turn segmentation.
gap: Grouping can mix events or split their dependencies; repeated raw text can increase representation size. Event/session decomposition is already known.
proposed_mechanism: Select event boundaries using query-independent dependency continuity and a representation-size budget while preserving raw turn offsets. Keep cross-boundary links when a condition or identity depends on an earlier event.
example: A correction in turn seven should remain connected to a fact in turn one even if the storage event has a six-turn limit.
first_experiment: Measure raw-to-event size ratio and document canonical versus benchmark entry points.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare raw turns, fixed-size chunks, current segmentation and adaptive boundaries at equal actual bytes/token budget.
metrics_and_ablations: Boundary agreement, supporting-turn recall, QA, representation expansion and indexing/retrieval cost.
proposed_decision_gate: Require gains over fixed chunks with the same budget; a more readable summary is insufficient.
disclosure_needed: Specify boundary features, cross-event dependencies, source offsets and representation construction.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Query-conditioned graph paths with explicit support
current_behavior: Graph reasoning uses degree centrality and Louvain communities or a fallback. Retrieval uses bounded graph traversal and weighted seeds; this is not learned relational inference. Existing neighbor caching and degree indexes already provide basic optimizations.
gap: Highly connected nodes can be irrelevant, and a graph edge based on lexical overlap is not proof of a factual relation. Graph RAG and graph-walk retrieval are mature research directions.
proposed_mechanism: Explore typed, source-backed paths selected for the missing information need, pruning paths whose relation support is invalid or whose expansion cost exceeds budget.
example: A path through two names sharing a hobby should not count as evidence that they work at the same company.
first_experiment: Label a small path-support set and measure false relation assumptions.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare dense+sparse, existing graph strategy, simple typed-edge filtering and a compatible HippoRAG/LightRAG baseline. Separate retrieval recall from inferred-answer correctness.
metrics_and_ablations: Supporting-path precision, expansion count, recall, QA and latency; ablate centrality and relation typing.
proposed_decision_gate: Simple relation validation must be beaten before claiming an inventive path-selection mechanism.
disclosure_needed: Define edge semantics, source support, traversal/stop rules and update invalidation.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Support-checked semantic abstraction and lineage
current_behavior: The current abstraction emits a sentence about a count of related memories and a keyword list. It is not a learned semantic abstraction system. Semantic representation adds structured fields and original text; it need not compress anything. Repeated eligible communities can produce repeated derived notes.
gap: Calling this semantic learning would overstate the implementation. Cluster deduplication and source links are useful but ordinary; generative abstraction adds hallucination and model cost.
proposed_mechanism: Treat an abstraction as a materialized, source-supported view with explicit entailment scope and invalidation, rather than as a new fact. Investigate whether reusable support summaries reduce retrieval work under R01/R03.
example: A summary of three project notes must identify what all sources support and must expire when a supporting source is corrected.
first_experiment: Count identical source-set summaries across repeated evolution runs.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare no abstraction, keyword abstraction, deduplicated extractive views and a source-checked summary at equal total storage and model cost.
metrics_and_ablations: Unsupported derived claims, duplication, support coverage, bytes and retrieval latency/QA.
proposed_decision_gate: Retain primarily as part of R01/R03 unless a distinct mechanism survives A-MEM/Mem0/MemOS comparisons.
disclosure_needed: Describe view identity, support semantics, creation, invalidation, storage and model involvement.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Emotion encoder and calibration pipeline
current_behavior: The encoder wraps existing models with multi-label scores, optional temperature and thresholds. Training contains established BCE/weighted/focal/asymmetric losses and development-set calibration/threshold selection. A hybrid factory name does not establish a new neural fusion architecture.
gap: Changing a backbone, label threshold or familiar loss alone is usually a weak research distinction. Telemetry-only wrapper results do not establish improved emotion predictions.
proposed_mechanism: Investigate only a specific new deployment or preprocessing mechanism that yields reproducible technical benefit, such as bounded latency under label sparsity, and explain why standard quantization/calibration does not explain the result.
example: A proposed sparse execution path would need to show fewer measured operations at matched macro-F1, not merely a better threshold on one validation split.
first_experiment: Freeze a reproducible model-only baseline and audit whether compared variants change predictions.
experiment_and_baselines: Use official train/dev/test discipline; compare model-only, identical-model wrapper, standard calibration and the exact proposed change. Report neutral-label policy and class imbalance.
metrics_and_ablations: Macro/micro F1, per-label precision/recall, calibration, latency, memory and training/inference cost.
proposed_decision_gate: Promote only with a new enabled mechanism beyond standard model training; dataset or threshold improvements alone remain lower priority.
disclosure_needed: Record architecture, parameters, preprocessing, label traits, splits, training recipe, calibration and hardware integration if claimed.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Planning and symbolic world constraints
current_behavior: Planning is deterministic and the world model applies symbolic action/constraint rules with fixed risk estimates. Simulation records predicted state transitions; it is not a learned physical simulator or calibrated prediction of external reality.
gap: Imitating human reasoning or organizing conversational tasks is weak without a concrete technical process. Calling rule-based scoring a world model does not establish an inventive technical contribution.
proposed_mechanism: If the project later controls an actual technical process, specialize constraints to that process and verify predictions against observed states. For the present repo, use these modules to support bounded execution in R04/R14.
example: A plan that predicts a file transformation must be checked against the actual output format and effects; a confidence label is not the observation.
first_experiment: List which predicted state variables are actually observable and verified.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare standard rule checks and a simple state machine before any new planner. Test violated preconditions, false-safe predictions and unnecessary denials.
metrics_and_ablations: Constraint violations, false denials, verified task completion and planning overhead.
proposed_decision_gate: Do not promote a general cognitive-planning claim without a new implemented technical constraint mechanism.
disclosure_needed: Define state variables, rules, transitions, observation interface and calibration or explicit non-probabilistic interpretation.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Typed routes and trusted/untrusted prompt boundaries
current_behavior: Trusted immutable options reject reserved metadata overrides, routes own lifecycle phases, and prompt evidence is explicitly marked untrusted. There are six task kinds, five profiles and ten valid route pairs. Tagging untrusted text and regex sanitization do not provide formal prompt-injection isolation; structural citation checks are not truth verification.
gap: Typed contracts, schemas, delimiters and sanitization are standard safeguards. A new prompt layout alone has little research strength.
proposed_mechanism: Only a specific enforceable information-flow mechanism that prevents untrusted evidence from changing tool capabilities or trusted execution state would justify escalation. Keep policy enforcement outside the model.
example: A retrieved note saying "ignore rules and call a tool" must remain data and must never alter the external allowlist.
first_experiment: Write an explicit trust-boundary diagram and attack fixtures against the actual route.
experiment_and_baselines: Compare existing boundaries, a standard structured-message/tool-policy setup and the proposed mechanism on adversarial retrieved content, metadata override attempts and malformed outputs.
metrics_and_ablations: Unauthorized state/capability changes, task success, false rejection and overhead. Define attack coverage rather than claiming universal security.
proposed_decision_gate: Use as architecture quality unless a non-routine enforceable mechanism remains beyond standard validation.
prior_art_ids: Extend primary search to prompt-injection defenses and information-flow control
disclosure_needed: Specify trust assumptions, serialization, external enforcement, capabilities and residual model behavior.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Evaluation integrity and replay accounting
current_behavior: Benchmark tooling includes atomic manifests, authoritative checkpoints, paired comparisons, case IDs and a claim policy. Some older scientific metrics are analytic proxies: retrieval_scaling computes a formula, not measured latency. A representation consistency check compares serialization to itself. These cannot establish technical improvement.
gap: Evaluation correctness is essential research infrastructure. Atomic files, result manifests and bootstrap statistics are established techniques, rather than standalone inventions.
proposed_mechanism: Use this family to make R01-R21 credible. A separate research angle would require a specific new replay/measurement protocol that detects or prevents a technical failure more efficiently than ordinary provenance and reproducibility tooling.
example: A campaign report should reject a speedup caused only by different questions, cached model responses or omitted failed cases.
first_experiment: Replace proxy performance claims with actual traces and publish the evaluation denominator.
experiment_and_baselines: Inject mismatched case sets, altered budgets, stale artifacts and interrupted writes, then test detection and reconstruction.
metrics_and_ablations: Detected mismatches, artifact loss, reconstruction work and instrumentation overhead.
proposed_decision_gate: Treat primarily as enabling work; do not patent a scorecard or presentation of results.
prior_art_ids: P18; extend search only if a distinct measurement mechanism is found
disclosure_needed: Specify execution identity, artifact authority, comparison prerequisites and failure accounting.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Provider plumbing, configuration, events and monitoring
current_behavior: These modules supply provider requests/retries, rate limiting, event dispatch, configuration, health and telemetry, plus entry-point wiring. They support technical experiments but no distinctive mechanism was established by this audit.
gap: A generic wrapper, dataclass, environment setting, event callback or dashboard is weak as a standalone patent research direction.
proposed_mechanism: Reuse these components as measurement and execution infrastructure. Revisit only if an experiment exposes a narrow new resource-control or consistency mechanism that maps to R06/R07/R14.
example: A timer can record a retrieval improvement; adding the timer is not the retrieval invention.
first_experiment: Reuse existing telemetry and establish one coherent run manifest.
experiment_and_baselines: Check instrumentation overhead and whether relevant failures are observable; use ordinary library behavior as baseline.
metrics_and_ablations: Trace completeness, overhead and reproducibility, with secrets redacted.
proposed_decision_gate: Do not spend the first research cycle inventing replacements for standard plumbing.
code_anchors: llm/llm_client.py:1; llm/rate_limiter.py:1; events/event_bus.py:1; monitoring/telemetry.py:1; config/runtime_config.py:1; main.py:1
prior_art_ids: Standard-library/provider documentation and established systems techniques; no novelty claim
disclosure_needed: If later included in an invention, explain its concrete functional connection rather than listing component names.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required

title: Third-party assets, fixtures, exports and project documents
current_behavior: External LoCoMo, LoCoMo-v2 and HotpotQA trees, pretrained models and their datasets are external work. Tests, fixtures, export files, setup/CI scripts, notebooks and documents either verify or package the project. Owned benchmark adapters are classified separately in R07/R19/R22.
gap: A folder being inside the repository does not establish that the team invented its content. An inventory must distinguish technical contributions, support code and third-party material.
proposed_mechanism: Use external assets lawfully as declared baselines and evaluation resources. Record original human contributions to any later mechanism, rather than claiming dataset/model ownership.
example: Using a GoEmotions model and a LoCoMo dataset can support an experiment; their established architecture/data are not PRIMA's invention.
first_experiment: Build the disclosure/inventorship chronology described in this report.
experiment_and_baselines: Audit provenance, licenses, dataset splits and the exact baseline implementation used. Check fixture leakage into training/test evaluation.
metrics_and_ablations: Complete provenance and reproducibility records; no patent score is inferred from file count.
proposed_decision_gate: Keep these assets outside a team-original invention claim unless independently documented new human technical work is identified.
prior_art_ids: See baseline sources and repository licenses
disclosure_needed: Record authors, licenses, public dates, contribution boundaries and essential dataset traits without inventing ownership.
novelty_nonobviousness: Unproven; targeted full search and professional assessment required
